newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians see gloomy 1997 after a hard 1996.
newsitem.headline: Russians see gloomy 1997 after a hard 1996.

text.p: Most Russians are gloomy about the prospects for themselves and their country in 1997 and see little chance of any changes for the better, a survey published on Thursday showed.

The opinion poll, carried out in the last week of December, showed that 56.7 percent of respondents thought 1997 would be a hard year for Russia and another 17 percent thought it would be extremely difficult.

A total of 55.1 percent of 2,200 respondents across Russia said 1996 had been hard, the poll showed. It was conducted by the Russian Independent Institute for Social and National Issues and published in the Nezavisimaya Gazeta daily.
A further 36.2 percent said it had been a very bad year.
Optimists made up 14 percent, evaluating 1997 prospects between good and excellent. Only four percent said last year was favourable or very good.
The majority expected a post-communist crime wave and corruption to rise this year, a decline in industry to continue and the number of unemployed to grow.
More than half the people asked said Russia's international prestige would deteriorate in 1997 and expected inter-ethnic problems within the vast Russian Federation to become more acute.
